canvas.reset:
Reset the application:
• fullscreen → windowed
• window size and position
• dark mode → light
• sidebar → visible / default width
• minimap → hidden
• icon and thumbnail size → normal
• font size → default
• language → automatic detection
• window split → 50 / 50
• renumbering → auto
• automatic straightening → manual
• ZIP compression → none

distillat.title: Have you heard of Distillat?
distillat.body:
Book 8 of your favorite saga just came out, and you're dying to read it. Except book 7 was 4 years ago, and your memories are a bit fuzzy: who were those secondary characters again? And what happened at the end?

If this sounds familiar, Distillat is for you. Simply drop your EPUB or PDF file into the designated area: you get a summary, character sheets, and an analysis of the work, ready to view or export to PDF.

The application relies on Gemini 3.5 Flash's free tier.

zip_compression.title: Default ZIP compression level
zip_compression.explanation:
Comic images are already compressed by their own format (JPEG, PNG, WebP...). Compressing the ZIP archive on top of that brings no space savings, but noticeably slows down saving and reading. That's why the default level is 0 (no compression).

Changing this setting is not recommended, unless you have a specific need.

help.title: MosaicView - User Manual
help.intro: MosaicView allows you to manipulate and edit comics (digital comics) without having to extract them from their archives. The application supports CBZ (ZIP), CBR (RAR) and PDF formats. The application is compatible only with 64-bit systems.
help.open_files_content:
• Click the 'Open a file' button or drag and drop a file directly into the window
• Supported formats: CBZ, CBR, CB7, CBT, PDF, images (JPG, PNG, WEBP, BMP, TIFF, GIF, ICO). EPUB files can also be opened, but only their images will be extracted (text is ignored). Note: extensions displayed in red (WEBP, TIFF, GIF, ICO…) indicate formats potentially incompatible with older CBZ/CBR readers. These files are nevertheless processed normally by MosaicView.
• Encrypted PDF (password required to open): the file cannot be imported, an error message is displayed.
• PDF protected against modifications (owner password): pages are imported normally. MosaicView offers to save an unlocked copy of the file in the same folder.
• Duplicate page detection: on opening an archive, pages with strictly identical content (a scanning or merging error) are automatically flagged with an orange badge on their thumbnail. "Manage duplicates" (Edit menu, right-click on the mosaic, or right-click on a thumbnail) opens a window listing every group of identical pages, with a checkbox per page to delete the extras.
help.mosaic_content:
The mosaic displays all pages of your comic book as thumbnails. You can:
• Rearrange pages by drag-and-drop (page renumbering will be automatic, and will follow the active renumbering mode)
• Select multiple pages (Ctrl+click or Shift+click)
• Adjust thumbnail size with the slider or Ctrl+scroll wheel
• Manually rename files by clicking on their name
• Drag-and-drop comic book files (CBZ/CBR/PDF) from Windows Explorer directly into another open comic book to merge their content
• Export all displayed thumbnails to a folder of your choice (hidden command, accessible only via the shortcut Ctrl+Alt+T)
• Show minimap: an optional side panel to the right of the mosaic showing a miniature overview of all pages, with a rectangle marking the currently visible area. Click or drag to navigate straight to that spot in the comic. Toggle it from the System menu or the right-click context menu on the mosaic.
help.manipulation_content:
• Drag and drop pages to reorganize them
• Drag an entire comic into another to merge them
• Right-click on a page to access options (rotation, deletion, etc.)
• Double-click on a page to open the viewer
• Export individual pages by dragging them to a Windows folder, or via Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V
help.renumber_content:
MosaicView offers three page renumbering modes, accessible via the renumbering button, the context menu (right-click), the status bar indicator, or automatically during drag and drop:

• Multi-page auto-detect mode (default): the application analyses the width of each page to detect double, triple pages, etc. Multi-pages are renumbered accordingly (e.g. a double page is named 003-004, a triple 005-006-007). Beyond 4 pages, only the first and last numbers are shown (e.g. 010---025).

• Simple enumeration mode: each page receives a unique sequential number (001, 002, 003...), regardless of page width.

• OFF mode: automatic renumbering is disabled. Original filenames are kept, including during drag and drop.

To switch between modes, right-click the renumbering button or click the indicator at the bottom right of the status bar. A tooltip shows the active mode in both cases. The selected mode also applies to automatic renumbering during drag and drop, and is remembered between sessions.
help.flatten_content: If your archive contains subdirectories, use 'Flatten directories' to bring all images to the same level.
help.viewer_content:
Double-click on a page to open the viewer:
• ← → keys: navigate between pages
• D key: switch between 4 reading modes
  - Single page: one page at a time
  - Double pages: page 1 alone, then 2-3, 4-5, etc.
  - Continuous double pages: page 1 alone, then 2-3, 3-4, 4-5, etc.
  - Webtoon: for vertical images (webcomics), width capped at 900px to stay readable; the mouse wheel scrolls vertically within the page, then turns the page once at the top/bottom
• Mouse wheel: quick navigation (vertical scroll within the page in Webtoon mode)
• Ctrl+Wheel or Ctrl+Plus/Minus: zoom (up to 1000% of the image's real size)
• Ctrl+0: fit zoom to the window
• Ctrl+1: zoom to 100% (real pixel size of the image)
• Right-click + drag: pan the displayed image when it exceeds the window
• F11 key: fullscreen
• Double-click: toggle fullscreen
• Esc key: cancel the current tool's drawing (crop, straighten, shape…) or exit the viewer
• Bookmark: automatically saves the current page when closing the viewer (except the first and last pages). A red ribbon appears on the corresponding thumbnail in the mosaic. On the next opening, a message suggests returning to this page. Automatically deleted on the last page, or manually via right-click in the viewer.

Floating toolbar: hover over the top of the image to reveal it (it hides itself after a few seconds). Click an icon to activate the matching tool:
• Crop: draw a rectangle, adjust it by its edges, validate; right-click the icon to switch to crop mask mode (memorize a rectangle with "Save mask", then recall it as-is on the following pages with "Recall mask" — handy for applying the same crop to several pages without redrawing it each time; "Forget mask" clears the memorized rectangle, page by page only)
• Straighten: draw a line on what should be horizontal/vertical, the correction applies automatically; right-click the icon to switch to automatic straightening (detects the skew on its own, no line to draw)
• Rotate/flip: one click rotates or flips the page
• Clone: Ctrl+click to set the source point, then paint with the mouse held down to duplicate
• Blur stamp: hold the left mouse button down and move the mouse over the area to blur (size and strength adjust independently); the effect stacks up if you go over the same spot again
• Text: click to place a text block, choose font/size/color
• Shapes: draw ellipses, rectangles, lines or arrows, with handles to resize them
• Sliders (sharpness, brightness/contrast, saturation, remove colors, compression): the result is shown live as you drag
• Levels: adjust black point/gamma/white point with sliders, or pick a color directly on the image with the eyedroppers
• Transparency: click a color on the image to make it transparent
• Color depth, Effects, Image mode: pick an option by clicking a radio button, applied immediately
• Paste an image: pastes the image from the clipboard (the icon only lights up if the clipboard holds an image), with handles to resize/rotate it like shapes; also works by dragging a page from a mosaic or a file from Windows Explorer straight onto the viewer. Ctrl+C copies the page being viewed (single page or Webtoon mode only), Ctrl+V pastes an image, same as in the mosaic

Validate with the "Validate" button when it appears, or Esc to cancel. Every change joins the usual Undo/Redo history.
help.join_pages_content:
Select multiple consecutive pages, right-click → 'Join selected pages' to join pages horizontally or vertically. The output image format matches the source pages' format if they are all identical, otherwise PNG by default. You'll be able to choose whether to delete or keep the original pages.

Where the new page lands in the mosaic:
• Active renumbering mode (auto or manual): the page takes the place of the first joined page (its place, if source pages are deleted, or right before it, if they're kept), and triggers a renumbering.
• OFF renumbering mode: the page is added at the front of the mosaic under the name "Merged_xxx".
help.split_pages_content:
To automatically split double pages:
• Select the pages to split
• Right-click → 'Split selected pages'
• Choose the direction (vertical or horizontal)
help.shortcuts_content:
• Ctrl+Z: Undo last action
• Ctrl+Y: Redo undone action
• Ctrl+A: Select all pages
• Ctrl+I: Invert selection
• Ctrl+C: Copy selected pages
• Ctrl+X: Cut selected pages
• Ctrl+V: Paste pages
• Del: Delete selected pages
• Ctrl+scroll wheel: Zoom (viewer) / thumbnail size (mosaic) / icon size (icon column)
• Ctrl+0 (viewer): Fit zoom to window
• Ctrl+1 (viewer): Zoom to 100% (real image size)
• Right-click + drag (viewer): Pan the displayed image
• Ctrl+Alt+T: Export all displayed thumbnails from the mosaic
• F5: Update the mosaic display
• F11: Toggle fullscreen (exit with F11 or ESC)
help.dark_mode_content: Click the sun/moon button to switch between light and dark themes.
help.sort_content:
Use the 'Sort' button to automatically reorganize pages by:
• Name, Type, Size, Width, Height, Resolution or DPI
help.save_content:
• 'Save': saves changes to the original file
• 'Save as': creates a new archive
• 'Create CBZ': available in images-only mode (without archive)

In all cases, saving is always done in CBZ format, at the default ZIP compression level. It is recommended to leave this level at 0. See the ZIP Compression section for more details.
help.other_content:
• Rotation: rotate one or more pages
• Conversion: convert images to different formats (PNG, JPEG, WEBP, BMP, TIFF, GIF). Note: CMYK images are automatically converted to RGB
• Printing: print selected pages or all pages
• Extraction: extract specific pages
help.config_files_content:
MosaicView stores temporary files in the {temp_dir} folder, needed for the various image processing operations while in use.
These files are deleted every time the application closes. You can also delete them manually by going to the {temp_dir} folder, or by clicking the buttons below: they will be recreated as needed.
help.config_temp_cleared: Temporary files have been successfully deleted.
help.config_config_cleared:
Configuration file has been successfully deleted.
It will be recreated on next application startup.
help.language_content:
MosaicView is available in multiple languages.
By default, the application automatically detects your operating system's language and displays in that language if supported. If your system uses an unsupported language, the interface displays in English.
You can manually change the language at any time using the dropdown menu located at the bottom of the button column, below the thumbnail size slider. Your choice will be saved and applied the next time you start the application.
AVAILABLE LANGUAGES: Arabic, Armenian, Bulgarian, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latvian, Lithuanian, Malay, Maltese, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Romanian, Slovak, Slovenian, Spanish, Swedish, Tamil, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese.
FICTIONAL LANGUAGES AVAILABLE: klingon (Latin alphabet and pIqaD alphabet versions), sindarin (Latin alphabet and tengwar alphabet versions), quenya (Latin alphabet and tengwar alphabet versions).

This utility uses Windows fonts, except for pIqaD (Klingon language) and tengwar (Elvish languages: Sindarin and Quenya) fonts. These fonts are free of rights and come from these sites:
- for pIqaD (Klingon language alphabet): {url_piqad}
- for tengwar (Elvish alphabet, for Sindarin and Quenya): {url_tengwar}
In case these sites are no longer active, you can retrieve the pIqaD and tengwar fonts by clicking on the buttons below:

This software was developed in French. Translations into other languages were done using AI, specifically Claude. I decided to support around forty languages. But obviously, I don't speak all these languages. Therefore, I had no choice but to use AI, as hiring and paying 40 different translators was not among the possibilities considered. Due to the automatic nature of these translations, errors may be present. I apologize for this.
help.credits_content: I know nothing about programming. Absolutely nothing. Consequently, I developed this software thanks to Claude, Anthropic's AI, and more precisely with Claude Code. I cannot recommend Claude Code enough, this application is fabulous!
help.resize_pages_content:
To reduce or enlarge your pages:
• Select one or more pages
• Right-click → 'Resize'
• Three options are available:
  - Custom dimensions: enter the desired width or height (aspect ratio is automatically preserved).
  - Percentage reduction: choose a percentage from 10% to 90%
  - Percentage enlargement: choose a percentage from 10% to 100%
• The application displays the estimated size of your images after modification
• The modification applies immediately to all selected pages
help.icons_content:
Most of the icons used in this utility come from this site and are free to use for non-commercial purposes: https://www.freepik.com/author/juicy-fish/icons/juicy-fish-sketchy_908#from_element=resource_detail
Some have been modified by me.
Only one icon, the Windows executable icon, was created by me (but with AI, because I'm a very, very, very bad graphic designer). You have my permission to use this icon as you wish as long as you cite your source.
help.split_ui_content:
MosaicView allows displaying two archives simultaneously, side by side.

Click the Split icon to open a second panel. Each panel is independent: you can open, edit and save an archive separately. The active panel is indicated by a blue border.

To move pages from one panel to the other, drag them directly. If multiple pages are selected, they all move together. Pages are inserted at the position indicated by the red bar.

Click the Close second panel icon to return to single-panel mode.

The separator bar between the two panels can be dragged freely. A double-click on it resets the panels to equal size (50/50).
help.config_clipboard_note: Exception: Temporary files used by the Windows clipboard (clipboard_XXXXX files) are kept for 12 hours after copying, so you can paste them even after closing the application. After 12 hours, they are automatically deleted.
help.config_log_note: Batch conversions (PDF to CBZ and CBR to CBZ) create a log file when an error occurs. These files (Log_pdftocbz_.txt and Log_cbrtocbz_.txt) are kept even after closing the application, so they can be reviewed later. They are only removed by the "Clear temporary files" button above. A Log_scan.txt file records every scan the same way (scanner used, settings, result or error) — useful for diagnosing a problem with your scanner.
help.config_clipboard_cleared: Clipboard files have been successfully cleared.
help.create_icon_content:
MosaicView allows you to create icon files (.ico) from any image in the mosaic.
• Right-click on an image → 'Create an icon'
• Frame the desired area in the viewer (the icon will be square)
• Adjust transparency if needed
• Confirm: the .ico file is added directly to the mosaic
• .ico files automatically contain all standard resolutions (from 16×16 to 256×256)
• As long as a .ico file is present in the mosaic, saving to a CBZ archive is blocked, as the ICO format is not supported by these archives. Export the .ico file separately (Ctrl+C then paste into a Windows folder), then delete it from the mosaic before saving.
help.batch_convert_content:
MosaicView offers eight batch conversion functions, available only when the mosaic is empty. The principle is the same for each: select a directory, confirm, follow the progress in real time, review the final summary. An option allows permanent deletion of the original files instead of sending them to the recycle bin.
• CBR → CBZ: converts all CBR (RAR) files in a directory and its subdirectories. If a CBR is actually a ZIP, 7z or TAR, the file is renamed with the correct extension without conversion. Renamed files and errors are logged.
• CB7 → CBZ: converts all CB7 (7-Zip) files in a directory and its subdirectories. If a CB7 is actually a ZIP, RAR or TAR, the file is renamed with the correct extension without conversion. Renamed files and errors are logged.
• CBT → CBZ: converts all CBT (TAR) files in a directory and its subdirectories. If a CBT is actually a ZIP, RAR or 7z, the file is renamed with the correct extension without conversion. Renamed files and errors are logged.
• PDF → CBZ: converts all PDF files in a directory and its subdirectories. Images are extracted without recompression.
• ISOLATED IMAGES → CBZ: creates an individual CBZ for each image file found in the directory and its subdirectories. Invalid, corrupted, multi-page (TIFF) or animated (GIF) images are ignored and logged.
• METADATA IMPORT: automatically retrieves metadata (title, series, authors…) from ComicVine for all compatible files (CBZ, CBR, CB7, CBT, PDF) in a directory and its subdirectories. A wizard opens successively for each file.
• CREATE LIBRARY: indexes all compatible files in a directory and its subdirectories into a new MosaicView library (*.mvdb). See the Library section for more details.
• RECOMPRESS CBZ FILES AT DEFAULT LEVEL: scans all CBZ, CBR, CB7 and CBT files in a directory and its subdirectories. The real format of each file is detected regardless of its extension: a mis-named file (for example a .cbr that is actually a ZIP) is renamed with the correct extension before being processed. Only true CBZ files are recompressed, and only if they are not already at the default compression level. The final summary shows the number of files analysed, recompressed, already at the default level, and ignored (not CBZ).
help.icon_toolbar_content: The icon toolbar provides quick access to the main functions of the application. You can rearrange the icons as you wish by dragging them directly in the toolbar. To choose which icons to show or hide, click the gear button at the bottom of the toolbar: a configuration window opens where you can move icons between the active toolbar and the reserve. Use the « + » and « − » buttons to adjust the size of the icons. The configuration is saved automatically.
help.nfo_editor_content:
An NFO file is a text file (with the .nfo extension) used to store information about the archive: synopsis, credits, notes…

To create an NFO file, use the dedicated icon in the toolbar, the File menu, or the context menu (right-click on the mosaic). The command is only available when the mosaic is not empty. Enter a name and content: the file is inserted directly into the mosaic, with no extraction or intermediate save.

To edit an existing NFO file, double-click it in the mosaic. The window opens pre-filled with the current name and content, both of which can be edited. In both cases, the operation is recorded in the undo history.
help.metadata_content:
MosaicView allows you to automatically retrieve metadata for your comics (title, series, number, authors, summary...) from the ComicVine database, a collaborative website maintained by the community.

Single mode: open a comic, then use the toolbar button or the Metadata menu. A two-step wizard opens: first choose the series, then the corresponding episode. Metadata is written to ComicInfo.xml inside the archive.

Batch mode: drop one or more folders onto the mosaic and choose "Batch metadata import", or use the dedicated toolbar button or the Metadata menu. The wizard opens successively for each file found (CBZ, CBR, CB7, CBT, PDF). Non-CBZ files are automatically converted to CBZ after the metadata is written.

API key: a free ComicVine API key is required. The application will guide you to obtain it. It is obtained at comicvine.gamespot.com after creating an account. The key is never stored in plain text: it is encrypted by Windows DPAPI and can only be read by your Windows account.

API limitations: these limitations are imposed by ComicVine and cannot be bypassed.
• 200 requests per resource per hour. If this limit is reached, searches temporarily fail until the end of the hour.
• Maximum 100 results per request, which forces searches to be split across multiple calls for series with many episodes.
• 1 request per second allowed by the site. For safety, MosaicView waits 2 seconds between each request, as faster requests are highly likely to cause temporary blocks.

ComicVine address formats: a ComicVine page address can appear in one of two formats depending on its age. MosaicView recognizes both interchangeably.
• Current format: comicvine.gamespot.com/.../4000-XXXXX for an issue, comicvine.gamespot.com/.../4050-XXXXX for a series.
• Old format: comicvine.com/.../37-XXXXX for an issue (the number after the dash is the same identifier; only the domain and prefix have changed).

This feature is entirely based on the open source project {scraper}.
help.library_content:
The library allows you to catalogue and easily find your digital comics. It works by reading the metadata contained in each file (title, series, authors, publisher…) and gathering them into a single library file (*.mvdb).

To create a library, use the Library menu → New database, or drop one or more folders into the mosaic and choose "Create a library from the folder(s)". MosaicView will then scan your folders and automatically index all compatible files.

Once the library is open, you can filter your comics by series, author, year, publisher, etc., combining as many criteria as needed. A double-click opens the file in MosaicView. Results can be exported in Excel format (*.xlsx).
help.zip_compression_content:
MosaicView lets you choose the ZIP compression level applied each time a CBZ is saved, accessible via the status bar indicator, the System menu, or the context menu (right-click on the canvas).

The default level is 0 (no compression): comic images are already compressed by their own format (JPEG, PNG, WebP...), so compressing the ZIP archive on top of that brings no space savings but noticeably slows down saving and reading. This level can be changed, but it is not recommended unless you have a specific need.

The status bar indicator shows the actual compression state of the open file: "0" if the file is not compressed, "1" if it is compressed (the ZIP format does not allow knowing the exact original level), or "--" if the file is not a CBZ. Left-clicking the indicator offers to resave the file (or convert it to CBZ) at the default level, when relevant. Right-clicking opens the default level settings window.
help.wilhelm_scream_content:
A handful of rare and severe errors trigger the famous Wilhelm scream, a sound effect used in hundreds of films and TV shows since the 1950s. If you don't know what it is, the Wikipedia page explains it very well: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelm_scream
The sound used in MosaicView comes from that page and was converted to WAV format so the application can play it.
help.config_single_instance_note: MosaicView never launches twice. If you open a file (by double-clicking it in Explorer, for example) while the application is already running, no second window appears: the file simply opens in the window that's already open, which is automatically brought to the front. For this to work, MosaicView registers itself with Windows on every launch (see below).
help.config_registry_note: To be able to appear in the Windows Explorer "Open with" menu, MosaicView writes a small amount of information to the Windows registry when it starts. This is kept to the strict minimum: it tells Windows where MosaicView is located and which file types it can open. It is only written to the part of the registry reserved for your user account, never the system-wide part, and it does not change any file association: choosing MosaicView as the default application for a file type remains a choice only you can make, through Windows' own "Open with" menu. If you remove MosaicView from your disk, this information simply becomes inactive and has no effect.
help.config_dir_content:
MosaicView creates a file named .mosaicview_config.json. This file contains the application's settings (window, theme, language, renumbering mode…), the list of recently opened comics and databases, your bookmarks, and your ComicVine API key (encrypted). It is located in the {config_dir} folder and is kept from one session to the next: unlike temporary files, it is never automatically deleted, neither by MosaicView nor by Windows.
You can delete it manually by going to the {config_dir} folder, or by clicking the button below. It will be recreated with default values the next time the application starts.
help.scan_content:
• Click the “Scan” button (icon column, File menu, or right-click on the mosaic) to open the scanning window. MosaicView drives your scanner directly (via WIA, the Windows scanning system): select the device, the resolution (DPI), the color mode (color / grayscale / black and white), then click “Scan”. A scanner must be plugged in, powered on, and its driver installed on Windows to appear in the list.
• The last scanner used, resolution, and color mode you chose are remembered and automatically proposed again the next time you scan.
• Only full-page scanning and exporting as JPG are offered, as the application already has everything needed for image editing and format conversion afterwards.
• The scanned image is automatically added to the mosaic, after the pages already present. You can then crop it, straighten it, adjust its colors, etc. like any other page in the mosaic
• This feature drives the scanner directly, without going through the manufacturer's software or displaying its own configuration window.
• Since a physical scanner can only be driven by one connection at a time, scanning is only possible in one panel at a time: if a scan window is open or a scan is in progress in one panel, the "Scan" button stays grayed out in the other panel until the operation finishes.
help.straighten_content:
Automatic straightening (no line to draw) is available from the icon column (right-click the "Straighten" icon to switch mode), the Images menu, or right-clicking the mosaic: it detects the skew on its own and straightens the selected page(s) directly; empty corners created by the rotation are filled in white. Works on several pages at once. A summary window shows how many pages were straightened successfully and lists the ones where no reliable skew could be detected.

Manual straightening (drawing a reference line) is done from the main viewer, see the Viewer section.
help.macro_content: The Macros tool («Record»/«Play» icons in the viewer toolbar) records a sequence of actions performed on a page and replays it identically on one or several others — from the viewer, or for several pages at once, from the mosaic (Images menu, right-click, icon column). A final report window lists pages processed successfully, partially, or failed, with the reason for each failure.

web.web_no_images_found: No images were found on this page.
web.web_copy_paste_message:
Direct drag & drop from web browser is not supported.

Alternative solution (simpler):

1. Right-click on the image in your browser
2. Choose 'Copy image'
3. In MosaicView, use the 'Paste' button or Ctrl+V

This method works with all web images!
web.web_drop_no_images_message: No image was found on this page.
web.web_drop_forbidden_message:
The site refused the connection (error 403).

Some sites block automated downloads. Try opening the page in your browser and copying the image directly (right-click → Copy image, then Ctrl+V in MosaicView).
web.web_drop_error_message: Could not retrieve this page's content. Check your Internet connection or the link address.
web.import_web_tooltip: Paste an internet address to retrieve all images from the page
web.import_web_dialog_title: Import images from a web page
web.import_web_invalid_url: Invalid URL. Please enter a valid web address.

donation.title: Make a donation
donation.message:
You like this little utility, and you use it regularly. I've invested several hundred hours into it. Would you consider thanking me by making a donation? Be nice, I really need money to fill my swimming pool with champagne.

Whether you want to send me a few cents or several billion euros, I accept all amounts. You can make this donation through paypal

mail.tooltip: This button opens your default email software in Windows to send an email. If no software is configured (for example if you use only webmail), you can copy the MosaicView address to the clipboard by right-clicking on the icon.

api_key_dialog.title: ComicVine API Key
api_key_dialog.explanation: To retrieve metadata for your comics, MosaicView uses the ComicVine database. You need a free API key.
api_key_dialog.instructions: Create an account on {comicvine}, then go to the {api_page} to get your key.
api_key_dialog.encryption_notice: Your key is never stored in plain text. It is protected by Windows DPAPI encryption, tied to your session.

comicvine.info_single: This function retrieves metadata for the currently open comic. To process multiple files at once, use batch processing (drop a folder onto the window).
comicvine.error_network_connection: Could not reach ComicVine. Check your Internet connection.
comicvine.error_network_timeout: ComicVine is taking too long to respond. Please try again shortly.
comicvine.error_api_invalid_key: Your ComicVine API key is not valid. Check it in the preferences.
comicvine.error_api_not_found: No data found on ComicVine for this request.
comicvine.error_api_url_format: Internal error in the request sent to ComicVine (invalid address format).
comicvine.error_api_jsonp: Internal error in the request sent to ComicVine (invalid response format).
comicvine.error_api_filter: Internal error in the search criteria sent to ComicVine.
comicvine.error_api_subscriber_only: This ComicVine content is for subscribers only.
comicvine.error_api_rate_limit: ComicVine request limit reached. Wait a few minutes before trying again.

comicvine_url.intro: You can load the metadata directly from a ComicVine page if you know its exact address, or continue to the search.
comicvine_url.hint_series: You can also paste the address of the whole series: you will then be able to choose the issue from the list.
comicvine_url.warning: Make sure this address really corresponds to the right series and issue.
comicvine_url.error_invalid_url: This address does not look like a valid ComicVine page (series or issue).
comicvine_url.error_not_found: No data found at this address.
comicvine_url.download_done_message: The metadata was downloaded and saved successfully.

scan.tooltip: Scan an image from a scanner and add it to the mosaic
scan.no_devices_found: No scanner was detected. Check that it is plugged in, powered on, and that its driver is installed.
scan.error_wia_unavailable: Unable to access the Windows scanning system. Check that a scanner driver is installed on this computer.
scan.error_enumeration_failed: An error occurred while searching for available scanners.
scan.error_device_unreachable: The selected scanner is no longer accessible. Check that it is still plugged in and powered on.
scan.error_no_scan_item: This scanner does not offer any usable scanning source.
scan.error_no_paper: No paper detected. Place a document on the scanner and try again.
scan.error_transfer_failed: The scanner did not respond correctly and the scan failed. Try again, or check the scanner.
scan.error_invalid_image: The image received from the scanner is invalid or damaged.
scan.send_log_link: Send the scan log by email
scan.no_log_yet: No scan has been performed yet: there is no log to send.
scan.mail_body_hint: Press Ctrl+V, or right-click then Paste, to send the scan log that was just copied.
scan.escl_fallback_hint: If the manufacturer's driver does not respond, Windows can sometimes scan directly.
scan.escl_fallback_button: Try with the generic Windows driver
